title: Finite monoid generators in rational tensor coordinates
statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group with a finite integral basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, meaning that every $g\in G$ has unique coordinates $g=\sum_k\lambda_k(g)e_k$ with $\lambda_k(g)\in\mathbf Z$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_m\in G$ generate $G$ as a group, meaning that every element is an integer combination of the $p_j$, and put $P=\{\sum_j a_jp_j:a_j\in\mathbf N\}$. Set $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with its rational vector-space structure from extension of scalars [def-weil-module-base-change], and $i(g)=g\otimes1$. Let $C$ be the set of all finite sums $\sum_\ell q_\ell i(u_\ell)$ with $u_\ell\in P$ and $q_\ell\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$. For each $k$ there is a unique $\mathbf Q$-linear map $L_k:V\to\mathbf Q$ with $L_k(g\otimes q)=q\lambda_k(g)$, and every $x\in V$ has the unique expansion $x=\sum_k L_k(x)i(e_k)$. Moreover $C=\{\sum_j q_ji(p_j):q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}$. For every integer matrix $(b_{kj})$ satisfying $e_k=\sum_j b_{kj}p_j$, and every $x\in V$, put $c_j=\sum_k L_k(x)b_{kj}$. Then $$x=\sum_j\max(c_j,0)i(p_j)-\sum_j\max(-c_j,0)i(p_j).$$ Empty bases and empty generating families are allowed; when $m=0$, $G=V=0$ and the displayed sums are zero.

proof.text: Regard $G$ as a $\mathbf Z$-module by integer multiplication. Uniqueness of the given integral expansion implies $\lambda_k(g+h)=\lambda_k(g)+\lambda_k(h)$ and $\lambda_k(ng)=n\lambda_k(g)$: adding the expansions, or multiplying one by $n\in\mathbf Z$, gives the corresponding expansion, so uniqueness identifies its coefficients. In particular $\lambda_k(e_h)=\delta_{kh}$. Thus $\beta_k(g,q)=q\lambda_k(g)$ is $\mathbf Z$-bilinear. Apply the tensor universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] to obtain the unique $\mathbf Z$-linear map $L_k:V\to\mathbf Q$ with $L_k(g\otimes q)=q\lambda_k(g)$.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product and its proof (universal property and pure-tensor generators); agent finite-coordinate and finite-sum calculations using Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product.

proof.text: This $L_k$ is $\mathbf Q$-linear. For fixed $a\in\mathbf Q$, the two maps $x\mapsto L_k(ax)$ and $x\mapsto aL_k(x)$ are $\mathbf Z$-linear. On $g\otimes q$ they agree, because the action in [def-weil-module-base-change] gives $a(g\otimes q)=g\otimes aq$, and both values are $aq\lambda_k(g)$. Pure tensors generate $V$ as a $\mathbf Z$-module by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so the maps agree everywhere. Uniqueness among $\mathbf Q$-linear maps with the required pure-tensor values follows from the same generation assertion, since a $\mathbf Q$-linear map is $\mathbf Z$-linear.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product and its proof (universal property and pure-tensor generators); agent finite-coordinate and finite-sum calculations using Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product.

proof.text: Put $E(x)=\sum_k L_k(x)i(e_k)$, a $\mathbf Q$-linear endomorphism of $V$. Bilinearity in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the scalar action in [def-weil-module-base-change] give, for each pure tensor, $$g\otimes q=\sum_k e_k\otimes(\lambda_k(g)q)=\sum_k q\lambda_k(g)i(e_k)=E(g\otimes q).$$ Pure-tensor generation now gives $E(x)=x$ for every $x$. If also $x=\sum_k d_ki(e_k)$ with rational $d_k$, applying $L_h$ gives $L_h(x)=\sum_k d_k\lambda_h(e_k)=d_h$. Thus the expansion is unique.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product and its proof (universal property and pure-tensor generators); agent finite-coordinate and finite-sum calculations using Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product.

proof.text: For $x\in C$ choose a defining finite expression $x=\sum_\ell q_\ell i(u_\ell)$, and write $u_\ell=\sum_j a_{\ell j}p_j$ with $a_{\ell j}\in\mathbf N$, as allowed by the definition of $P$. Bilinearity and extension of scalars give $$x=\sum_\ell\sum_j q_\ell a_{\ell j}i(p_j)=\sum_j\left(\sum_\ell q_\ell a_{\ell j}\right)i(p_j).$$ Each parenthesized coefficient is nonnegative rational, since every summand is. Conversely $p_j\in P$ (its coefficient vector has a single $1$), so any $\sum_j q_ji(p_j)$ with $q_j\ge0$ is a defining expression for $C$. The zero expression is the empty sum. This proves the cone equality without a cone-hull theorem.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product and its proof (universal property and pure-tensor generators); agent finite-coordinate and finite-sum calculations using Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product.

proof.text: Fix any integer matrix in the statement. Applying the additive map $i$ to its row identities gives $i(e_k)=\sum_j b_{kj}i(p_j)$. Substitute in the expansion already proved and reorder the finite sums: $$x=\sum_k L_k(x)\sum_j b_{kj}i(p_j)=\sum_j\left(\sum_k L_k(x)b_{kj}\right)i(p_j)=\sum_j c_ji(p_j).$$ For each rational $c$, $c=\max(c,0)-\max(-c,0)$: if $c\ge0$ the right side is $c-0$, and if $c\le0$ it is $0-(-c)$. Substitute this identity for each $c_j$ and distribute the finite sum to obtain exactly the asserted difference. Its two sums have nonnegative rational coefficients. Existence of such a matrix, when needed, follows by applying the group-generation hypothesis separately to each $e_k$.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product and its proof (universal property and pure-tensor generators); agent finite-coordinate and finite-sum calculations using Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product.

proof.text: No argument requires a nonempty index set. If $r=0$, the given integral expansion says every $g$ is the empty sum $0$; the expansion of Step 3 likewise says every $x\in V$ is $0$. If $m=0$, the group-generation hypothesis says every $g$ is an empty integer combination, so $G=0$; hence every pure tensor is $0$, and pure-tensor generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $V=0$. The only natural combination defining $P$ is $0$, so $C=\{0\}$; both sides of the cone equality and the signed formula are empty sums. If $r=0$ and $m>0$, all $p_j$ are zero and $c_j=0$, so the same conclusions hold.

lean.statement: theorem finite_monoid_rational_coordinates (G : Type u) [AddCommGroup G] (r m : ℕ) (e : Module.Basis (Fin r) ℤ G) (p : Fin m → G) (hp : ∀ g : G, ∃ a : Fin m → ℤ, g = ∑ j, a j • p j) (P : Set G) (hP : P = {g | ∃ a : Fin m → ℕ, g = ∑ j, a j • p j}) (C : Set (TensorProduct ℤ ℚ G)) (hC : C = {x | ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → G) (q : Fin n → ℚ), (∀ l, v l ∈ P) ∧ (∀ l, 0 ≤ q l) ∧ x = ∑ l, q l ⊗ₜ[ℤ] v l}) : ∃ L : Fin r → (TensorProduct ℤ ℚ G →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ), (∀ (k : Fin r) (g : G) (q : ℚ), L k (q ⊗ₜ[ℤ] g) = q * (e.repr g k : ℚ)) ∧ (∀ (k : Fin r) (L' : TensorProduct ℤ ℚ G →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ), (∀ (g : G) (q : ℚ), L' (q ⊗ₜ[ℤ] g) = q * (e.repr g k : ℚ)) → L' = L k) ∧ (∀ x : TensorProduct ℤ ℚ G, x = ∑ k, L k x • ((1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] e k)) ∧ (∀ (x : TensorProduct ℤ ℚ G) (d : Fin r → ℚ), x = ∑ k, d k • ((1 : ℚ) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] e k) → ∀ k, d k = L k x) ∧ C = {x | ∃ q : Fin m → ℚ, (∀ j, 0 ≤ q j) ∧ x = ∑ j, q j ⊗ₜ[ℤ] p j} ∧ (∀ b : Fin r → Fin m → ℤ, (∀ k, e k = ∑ j, b k j • p j) → ∀ x : TensorProduct ℤ ℚ G, x = (∑ j, max (∑ k, L k x * (b k j : ℚ)) 0 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] p j) - ∑ j, max (-(∑ k, L k x * (b k j : ℚ))) 0 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] p j) ∧ (m = 0 → (∀ g : G, g = 0) ∧ (∀ x : TensorProduct ℤ ℚ G, x = 0))
